(II)--a mind-born daughter of ब्रह्मा given to वज्राङ्ग, son of Diti and कश्यप; she performed penance with her husband when Indra disturbed her by assuming different fearful disguises. She represented this to her husband at the end of his penance, and was blessed with a son, तारक. When he vanquished Indra, she became pleased. M. १४६. ५८; Ch. १४७ (whole).

(I)--(विष्णु). (I)--(see मीत्रावरुण) King of the Asuras; when called upon to fight by हिरण्यकशिपु, he said that his passion was in a subdued state, and asked him to meet Hari in battle;

(सुनादेवी- वा। प्।) propitiated by हरिश्चन्द्र, वरुण gave him a son on condition that he offered him in a sacrifice to him. Though reminded a number of times, हरिश्चन्द्र evaded fulfilling his promise and consequently got the disease, महोदर। But his son Rohita purchased सुनश्शेप as his substitute. वरुण was pleased and relieved him of his disease.

--a वैष्णवी vidya1, taught by विश्वरूप to Indra. Here the various manifestations of Hari [page३-162+ २५] including that of the Buddha are recalled. Once a certain कौशिकन् practised this and gave up his life in a desert. When a Gandharva crossed the bones of this dead man, he fell down on the earth. Instructed by वालखिल्यस्, he collected the bones, and after throwing them into the सरस्वती, and bathing there, returned to his place. Taught originally to त्वष्ट्रि by Dadhyanga; त्वष्ट्रि taught it to विश्वरूप. भा.

--शिव addresses पार्वती on, in taking her out and showing the grandeur and majesty of the forest and garden round about काशी; the place of विद्या- [page३-198+ ४१] dharas, Siddhas and चारणस्. Here भगवान् Pin3gala became गणेश्वर and क्षेत्रपाल and distributor of food to the residents in the city. He was originally a यक्ष, son of पूर्णभद्र. He devoted himself to severe austerities and was blessed by शिव to be a गणपति.
1: M. ch. १८०.
It is अविमुक्त तीर्थ for here शिव is omnipresent and is never absent from there. All sinners who die here become Rudras in time. शिव stands here like a pillar, motionless till the deluge. Every part of the city is holy.
2: Ib. ch. १८१.
He who remains here for a month gets the benefit of observ- ing the पाशुपत vow. By living permanently one gets true emancipation. By giving up life at the मणिकर्णिका ghat one secures the desired goal. Perpetual life in काशी leads one to union with शिव.
3: Ib. ch. १८२.
काशी's importance on account of its sacred stream, the Ganges; survives all deluge; शिव addresses पार्- वती on the great glory of the क्षेत्रम् in terms of Parama- yoga, Paramagati and परममोक्ष. It is a place where people of all वर्णस् attain immortality. Gifts of cow and other things in this city are always beneficial.
4: Ib. ch. १८३.
It is the place where शिव got rid of the curse of ब्रह्मा to roam about with a skull for having cut off the fifth head of the creator. Through the grace of Hari, the skull fell down in काशी and broke into a thousand pieces.
5: Ib. ch. १८४.
It is the burial ground of all the gods, the ground being the Avimukta temple. It is the seat of ब्रह्मा. But it deludes non- devotees. Here वेदव्यास resided for १२ years observing the vow of silence. At the end of the vow he felt hungry and asked for alms. None was able to feed him. When he was about to curse the city, शिव and पार्वती took the human form and entertained him to his satisfaction. Then व्यास knew of his guests who remarked that a man of choleric temper like himself should not live in that city. But he was permitted to visit it twice a fortnight on अष्टमि and चतुर्दशी days.
6: Ib. ch. १८५.

--ब्रह्मा took the वारुणि body and offer- ed his शुक्र (semon) to Agni to beget sons; hence eight sons who are ऋषिस्; भृगु, Angiras, मरीचि, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri, and वसिष्ठ; all devas and यज्ञङ्गस् in the shape of human forms were present; also Vedas as well as लक्षण, svara, sthopa, nirukta, devakanyas, deva-patnis, देवमातरस्, all in human form. वा. ६५. १८-30.
